claims.assertion: The trip deviated from the optimal route twice: the GPS track shows off-route segment 18:40–18:45 adding 3.17 km and off-route segment 18:59–19:08 adding 4.78 km, totalling +8.5 km (+41%) over the 20.6 km optimal route.

Only the first deviation is covered by the rider's consent: the rider's agreement message at 18:38 ('Sure, go ahead') predates the 18:40–18:45 segment, which the driver had requested at 18:37 for the Bukit Timah Expressway jam.

The second deviation (18:59–19:08, adding 4.78 km) was never requested or agreed before it began: the driver's own statement concedes 'the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting', and no chat message proposes or consents to it.

No exemption applies to the second segment: traffic records list no incident anywhere near the route during the trip window and the weather was fair, so there is no 'reasonable cause' evidence for that off-route segment.
This was a metered RydeTAXI trip whose distance component is billed per km, so the 4.78 km of unexempted off-route driving entered the fare: distance fare $40.96 on 29.1 km, i.e. $1.41/km.

The refund is 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74 SGD, payable for the unexempted segment only; the $5.50 residual between the $11.96 total excess charge (8.5 km × $1.41) and the 8.0 km of measured segments is a map-matching residue and is not claimed.

The driver's account shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld within the window, and the 18:59–19:08 deviation the driver attributes to GPS rerouting is a second off-route event on one trip, so the account should additionally be sent to Ryde for review.

weaknesses: The first off-route segment (F3, 18:40–18:45, +3.17 km) was genuinely agreed in advance (F8 request 18:37, F9 agreement 18:38), so the rider cannot recover that segment and must concede it.

Traffic evidence (F11: BUKIT TIMAH EXPRESSWAY band 5, 40–49 km/h; F12: PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY band 4, 30–39 km/h) shows congestion on expressways during the whole trip window, which the driver will use to argue the second reroute was also for an operational reason rather than for extra fare — although F13 shows no incident on the route and RD-4(b) bands alone do not exempt a segment.

The driver will argue a single continuous reroute was authorised by the 18:38 agreement (F9); the rider's case on the second segment relies on RD-5's 'before you go' rule and on the 21-minute gap and 1687 m maximum distance from the route in F4.
Profile facts (F16 route_upheld_90d = 0) cannot decide the case and only support the flag_account request; the flag is an add-on, not the rider's substantive remedy.

[F3 F4 F8 F9 F10] [RD-1 RD-5 RD-3]
D3: The driver cannot justify the second segment as a congestion reroute: the only traffic record on a nearby expressway is a moderate band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Bukit Timah Expressway, no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and no speed band 1 or 2 (severe congestion) supports a second justified deviation. [F11 F12 F13 F14] [RD-4]
D4: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (base $3.90 + distance $40.96 for 29.1 km + time $11.40), so the refund for the single non-exempt segment is computed on the metered per-km rate: $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.40756/km; 4.78 km × $1.40756 = $6.73 SGD. [F5 F7] [RD-2 NS-0]

Asks: refund_partial $6.73

Only the second off-route segment (18:59–19:08, +4.78 km) is a non-exempt deviation, because the driver's reroute request and the rider's agreement concerned only the first turn-off around the jam near the start; the driver's own statement admits the second turn-off was GPS rerouting made at his own initiative.

weaknesses: The GPS record F1 shows the trip covered 29.0 km against a 20.6 km optimal route (+8.5 km, +41%) and F2 shows 43.8 min against 29 min, so on the face of the system records the whole trip was substantially longer than the shortest and most direct route required by RD-1; the rider will use F1 and F2 to argue the driver's routing was unjustified overall.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.74 (model confidence 0.87)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so deviation kilometres flow directly into the fare and RD-2's metered branch applies [F7][RD-2]. The GPS record shows two off-route segments, each of which must be examined separately under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F4][RD-1].

Segment 18:40–18:45 (+3.17 km): the driver named the route before leaving — "ok if I go round via Kranji Expressway?" at 18:37 — and the rider agreed "Sure, go ahead" at 18:38, both timestamps preceding the segment's 18:40 start [F8][F9][F3]. claims.assertion: The trip deviated from the optimal route twice: the GPS track shows off-route segment 18:40–18:45 adding 3.17 km and off-route segment 18:59–19:08 adding 4.78 km, totalling +8.5 km (+41%) over the 20.6 km optimal route.

Only the first deviation is covered by the rider's consent: the rider's agreement message at 18:38 ('Sure, go ahead') predates the 18:40–18:45 segment, which the driver had requested at 18:37 for the Bukit Timah Expressway jam.

The second deviation (18:59–19:08, adding 4.78 km) was never requested or agreed before it began: the driver's own statement concedes 'the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting', and no chat message proposes or consents to it.

No exemption applies to the second segment: traffic records list no incident anywhere near the route during the trip window and the weather was fair, so there is no 'reasonable cause' evidence for that off-route segment.
This was a metered RydeTAXI trip whose distance component is billed per km, so the 4.78 km of unexempted off-route driving entered the fare: distance fare $40.96 on 29.1 km, i.e. $1.41/km.

The refund is 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74 SGD, payable for the unexempted segment only; the $5.50 residual between the $11.96 total excess charge (8.5 km × $1.41) and the 8.0 km of measured segments is a map-matching residue and is not claimed.

The driver's account shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld within the window, and the 18:59–19:08 deviation the driver attributes to GPS rerouting is a second off-route event on one trip, so the account should additionally be sent to Ryde for review.

weaknesses: The first off-route segment (F3, 18:40–18:45, +3.17 km) was genuinely agreed in advance (F8 request 18:37, F9 agreement 18:38), so the rider cannot recover that segment and must concede it.

Traffic evidence (F11: BUKIT TIMAH EXPRESSWAY band 5, 40–49 km/h; F12: PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY band 4, 30–39 km/h) shows congestion on expressways during the whole trip window, which the driver will use to argue the second reroute was also for an operational reason rather than for extra fare — although F13 shows no incident on the route and RD-4(b) bands alone do not exempt a segment.

The driver will argue a single continuous reroute was authorised by the 18:38 agreement (F9); the rider's case on the second segment relies on RD-5's 'before you go' rule and on the 21-minute gap and 1687 m maximum distance from the route in F4.
Profile facts (F16 route_upheld_90d = 0) cannot decide the case and only support the flag_account request; the flag is an add-on, not the rider's substantive remedy.

claims.assertion: The first off-route segment (18:40–18:45, +3.17 km) is exempt: the driver proposed the reroute via Kranji Expressway at 18:37 and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead" at 18:38, i.e. before the segment started at 18:40, so the rider agreed in advance to that deviation.

Only the second off-route segment (18:59–19:08, +4.78 km) is a non-exempt deviation, because the driver's reroute request and the rider's agreement concerned only the first turn-off around the jam near the start; the driver's own statement admits the second turn-off was GPS rerouting made at his own initiative.

The driver cannot justify the second segment as a congestion reroute: the only traffic record on a nearby expressway is a moderate band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Bukit Timah Expressway, no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and no speed band 1 or 2 (severe congestion) supports a second justified deviation.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (base $3.90 + distance $40.96 for 29.1 km + time $11.40), so the refund for the single non-exempt segment is computed on the metered per-km rate: $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.40756/km; 4.78 km × $1.40756 = $6.73 SGD.

The waiting fee is $0.00 in the fare breakdown and the excess-distance line ($11.96 for 8.5 km) covers both segments, so no additional itemised charge beyond the recomputed metered distance attributable to the non-exempt segment should be refunded.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes with 1 upheld but 0 route disputes upheld, so the threshold that would make this case a 'repeated' route deviation (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no account flag is warranted.

weaknesses: The GPS record F1 shows the trip covered 29.0 km against a 20.6 km optimal route (+8.5 km, +41%) and F2 shows 43.8 min against 29 min, so on the face of the system records the whole trip was substantially longer than the shortest and most direct route required by RD-1; the rider will use F1 and F2 to argue the driver's routing was unjustified overall.

The driver's own statement F10 concedes the second turn-off was made without asking the rider, which the rider will combine with F4 to press for that segment's excess kilometres to be refunded under RD-2.

The driver's argument that the second deviation was necessary is unsupported: F13 records no traffic incidents near the route and F11/F12 show only moderate bands (5 and 4), so RD-4's 'reasonable cause' exception cannot be invoked.

The rider will argue under RD-3(b)/RD-5 that the consent in F9 was limited to the first Kranji detour and therefore did not cover the second off-route segment; the driver has no chat message dated before 18:59 seeking agreement to that second deviation.

points.response: Conceded: the rider's 18:38 agreement (F9) precedes the 18:40–18:45 segment (F3) in response to the driver's 18:37 request (F8), so under RD-5 that segment is exempt and no refund is sought for its 3.17 km.

Agreed, and it is the rider's own case: the unexempted segment is the 18:59–19:08 deviation adding 4.78 km (F4), which no message proposed or approved before 18:59 (F8, F9), so its extra kilometres are refundable under RD-2.

Agreed: with no incident on the route (F13), fair weather (F14) and only bands 5 and 4 on the expressways (F11, F12), there is no RD-4 cause for the second deviation, and RD-4(b) bands alone cannot exempt it.

Accepted in substance: the metered rate is $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.41/km (F7), so 4.78 km × $1.41 = $6.74, a 1-cent rounding difference from the driver's figure and immaterial to the rider; the rider's own $6.74 computation (F4, F5, F7) stands.

The refund is confined to the unexempted segment's kilometres ($6.74), so no waiting fee is claimed (F7 shows $0.00) and the rider already waives the $5.50 map-matching residue between the $11.96 excess line and the 8.0 km of measured segments (F5, F4).

The rider does not rely on the flag for the refund, but note F16 records 1 dispute upheld in 90 days and a driver with 883 trips in 90 days, and RD-6 turns on the overall record plus this infringement rather than on a route-specific count, so a review of the driver's routing conduct is properly attached to the refund.

Conceded to the extent it is a purely descriptive GPS statement: F1/F3/F4 do show two off-route segments, but RD-1 liability attaches segment by segment and the 18:40–18:45 segment is already exempted by the rider's own advance agreement (F8, F9), so the +8.5 km total is not an unexempted deviation.

Agreed without qualification: F8 (driver request 18:37) and F9 (rider "Sure, go ahead" 18:38) both predate the 18:40 start of that segment in F3, so under RD-5 that segment is no_action — this is exactly the driver's own D1.

Conceded: F10 admits the 18:59–19:08 turn-off was the driver's own response to GPS rerouting with no prior chat request, and RD-5 requires agreement before the deviation, so only the +4.78 km in F4 is non-exempt.

Conceded; RD-4 offers no exemption for the second segment because F13 records no incident near the route in the trip window, the fair weather in F14 rules out any weather cause, and RD-4(b)/G3 makes the band 4–5 speeds in F11/F12 corroborative only, never a standalone exemption.

Accepted that the trip was metered (F7) and that distance entered the fare, but the per-km rate must be taken from the metered components actually charged — $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.40756/km — rather than an assumed $1.41, which is the intermediate rounding the rider's C5/C6 rely on.

Conceded on substance and amount within a cent: the driver's Figures D4/D5 already request refund_partial for the single non-exempt segment only, 4.78 km × $1.40756 = $6.73, and the rider's waiver of the ≤0.25 km map-matching residue is consistent with RD-2, so the driver does not contest the rider's $6.74 but claims no further deduction.

Contested: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 for a flag_account add-on, and F16 shows 0 route disputes upheld (the single upheld dispute is not a route case), so the account-review threshold for a repeated route offence is not met even though this segment is upheld.
